1.name: Ritual Adept
1.description: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

2.name: Arcane Tradition
2.description: When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition from the list of available traditions, shaping your practice of magic. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

2.name: Scholar
2.description: While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Medicine}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}. You have Expertise in the chosen skill.

3.name: Cantrip Formulas
3.description: {@i 3rd-level wizard optional class features feature} You have scribed a set of arcane formulas in your spellbook that you can use to formulate a cantrip in your mind. 3.name: Wizard Subclass
3.description: You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Wizard level or lower.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat.html}.

5.name: Memorize Spell
5.description: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.
